decision: blocked design: do not implement or adopt based on this source-only review
findings: The sketched shared gate excludes the reviewed outstanding-reservation shutdown interleavings under stated ordinary send/wake and lifecycle assumptions. It is not an implementation or proof.

Permanent combined-capacity violations use InvalidConfig, temporary aggregate byte pressure uses Busy, and full/stopped/oversized precedence is documented as intended non-racing behavior. Both errors close real transport connections through HandlerError; buffer reuse and starvation effects remain to be tested.

Channel send/wake unwind, gate poisoning, reentrant destructors/wakers, receiver ownership and cancellation before startup remain blockers. Any rejected command, oneshot sender, reply, receiver drain or buffer destructor must be moved out of the synchronous gate before dropping.
The bound covers queued input capacities and transient charges; active jobs, outputs, unpolled/waiting callers, allocator overhead, buffers and RSS require separate accounting.
limitations: Python toy model and source checks only; no Cargo, compiler, native Rust/Tokio execution, actor/WAL/network test or benchmark.
The abstract state machine excludes multiple producers, byte-counter implementation, panic/poison, reentrancy, memory ordering, wake failure and scheduler fairness.
The post-close permit/oneshot hang remains a source-derived risk requiring deterministic Tokio reproduction, not an observed failure.
No production-readiness, release-readiness or performance conclusion.
